title: Financial Planning & Analysis Specialist
location_raw: United States of America, Washington, Liberty Lake
description:
Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us.

This role serves as a strategic finance partner to the Outcomes Research & Development (R&D) organization, enabling innovation and value creation within a technology-driven Utilities & Energy environment. The position provides end-to-end financial planning, analysis, and operational support across actuals, budgets, forecasts, and long-range plans. By delivering clear insights, scalable planning tools, and scenario-based analysis, this role helps R&D leaders make informed, customer-centric investment decisions. The role collaborates closely with the Project Management Office (PMO), engineering, and senior R&D and corporate leaders to support effective resource allocation, portfolio health, and continuous improvement.

Duties & Responsibilities

- Act as an accountable finance partner to the global R&D organization, supporting innovation initiatives that deliver long-term customer and business value in the Utilities & Energy sector.

- Prepare, analyze, and present monthly and quarterly financial reporting for global R&D spend, highlighting key drivers, variances, risks, and opportunities, and recommending agile corrective actions when needed.

- Lead and support the development of annual budgets, rolling forecasts, and long-range plans for R&D, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities, innovation roadmaps, and customer outcomes.

- Drive continuous improvement of R&D budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes, increasing transparency, efficiency, and cross-functional collaboration.

- Analyze R&D investment profiles at the project and portfolio level, evaluating spend efficiency, portfolio health, and the financial impact of new product development and innovation pipelines.

- Develop, maintain, and refine financial models that support scenario planning, investment governance, and executive-level decision-making.

- Partner closely with global R&D leaders, engineering teams, and the PMO to incorporate project updates, resource changes, and timeline shifts into financial plans and forecasts.

- Collaborate with R&D operating expense owners to ensure accurate forecasting, insightful variance analysis, and disciplined financial management tied to key strategic initiatives.

- Manage ad hoc reporting and analysis requests, validate data inputs, resolve discrepancies, and uphold high standards of financial accuracy and integrity.

- Support and lead strategic and operational initiatives related to R&D transformation, resource planning, and investment optimization, acting as a proactive change agent.

Required Skills & Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related business discipline.

- 3–5 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, or a related analytical finance role.

- Demonstrated ability to partner authentically with cross-functional stakeholders and influence decision-making through data-driven insights.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of accountability and attention to detail.

- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment while managing multiple priorities with agility.

- Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information to diverse audiences.

Preferred Skills & Experience

- MBA and/or PMP certification.

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with Power BI preferred.

- Advanced working knowledge of Oracle Cloud EPM Planning or a similar cube-based planning and reporting platform.

- Experience building and managing financial models to drive insight, support scenario planning, and identify optimization opportunities.

- Comfort challenging the status quo, influencing change, and driving continuous improvement in a collaborative, innovative culture.

- Strong organizational skills and the ability to drive progress in a hybrid work environment (virtual and in-office).

Benefits Info:
This position also includes a competitive benefit package including; financial, social, health and wellbeing programs, paid vacation, 401k matching, employee stock purchase program, hybrid work schedule, and more!

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills and experience and may vary by location. The base salary is $75,000-124,500 annually. This position is eligible for our annual bonus program.

title: DevOps Engineer
location_raw: United States of America, Illinois, Chicago
description:
Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us.

At Itron, we help utilities modernize critical infrastructure through digital solutions that connect the field, office, and enterprise. As part of our Locusview product line, our fast-growing Resiliency Solutions business, you'll combine the agility of a startup with the scale of an industry leader while helping drive the future of utility infrastructure.

Position Overview
The DevOps Engineer plays a critical role in designing, building, and maintaining the cloud infrastructure, automation frameworks, and deployment pipelines that power our technology platform. This individual partners closely with software engineering, product, and operations teams to deliver scalable, secure, and highly available solutions that support utility and energy customers. Success in this role requires a customer-centric mindset, strong technical expertise, continuous improvement, and a commitment to collaboration, accountability, and innovation.

Duties & Responsibilities

- Design, implement, and continuously improve CI/CD pipelines to accelerate software delivery while maintaining quality, security, and reliability.

- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to design, deploy, and optimize cloud-native infrastructure solutions that support business growth and customer success.

- Own and support production-grade environments, ensuring high availability, resiliency, performance, and operational excellence.

- Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) solutions using Terraform and industry best practices.

- Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize cloud infrastructure and services to proactively identify and resolve issues.

- Automate operational processes and repetitive tasks to improve efficiency, consistency, and scalability.

- Partner with development teams to enhance application deployment strategies, system architecture, and operational readiness.

- Contribute to a culture of continuous learning, innovation, accountability, and agile delivery.

- Act as a trusted technical partner, helping deliver reliable solutions that enable utility customers to modernize and strengthen critical infrastructure.

Required Skills & Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 4+ years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Cloud Engineering, or a related role supporting production environments.

- Hands-on experience with Docker and containerization technologies.

- Experience with container orchestration platforms, including Amazon ECS and/or Kubernetes (EKS).

- Strong knowledge of AWS services, including VPC, ECS, EKS, EC2, Route 53, S3, SQS, SNS, ElastiCache, OpenSearch, and AWS Transfer Family.

- Proven experience developing and managing Infrastructure as Code using Terraform, including creating and implementing reusable modules.

- Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitHub Actions, AWS CodePipeline, or similar technologies.

- Experience supporting and maintaining production infrastructure with a focus on reliability, scalability, and performance.

- Knowledge of cloud monitoring and security tools such as CloudWatch, CloudTrail, and GuardDuty.

- Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language, such as Python, Bash, Groovy, or similar.

- Strong problem-solving, analytical, and troubleshooting skills.

- Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, agile environment and communicate technical concepts clearly to diverse stakeholders.

- Demonstrated commitment to accountability, customer focus, and delivering high-quality results.

Preferred Skills & Experience

- Experience supporting SaaS platforms and large-scale cloud-native applications.

- Knowledge of observability, monitoring, and logging best practices.

- Experience implementing DevSecOps practices and cloud security frameworks.

- Familiarity with microservices architectures and distributed systems.

- Experience working within the Utilities, Energy, Infrastructure, Telecommunications, or related industries.

- Knowledge of application performance monitoring and incident management processes.

- AWS certifications (e.g., Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer, SysOps Administrator) or equivalent cloud certifications.

- Experience optimizing infrastructure costs and improving operational efficiency.

- Passion for technology innovation and helping customers solve complex operational challenges.

- Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment while fostering authentic and collaborative relationships.

title: Principal, AI Security
location_raw: United States of America, Texas, Austin; United States of America, Washington, Liberty Lake; United States of America, Illinois, Chicago; United States of America, South Carolina, West Union; United States of America, North Carolina, Raleigh
description:
Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us.

Itron, Inc. (NASDAQ: ITRI) is a global leader in technology and services dedicated to the resourceful use of energy and water. With more than 300 million connected endpoints deployed worldwide, Itron is one of the world's largest and most successful IoT companies. Through innovative technology, software, and services, we help utilities and cities improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and build a more resourceful and sustainable future.

As we accelerate adoption of artificial intelligence across our enterprise, products, and services, we are seeking an exceptional security leader to help shape and secure the future of AI at Itron.

Role Summary

The Principal, AI Security Architecture & Engineering serves as Itron's senior technical authority for AI security. This highly visible, hands-on leadership role is responsible for defining and implementing the security architecture, governance controls, engineering standards, and operational practices that enable safe, scalable adoption of artificial intelligence, generative AI, machine learning, and AI agents across the enterprise and product portfolio.
The ideal candidate combines deep cybersecurity expertise with practical experience securing modern AI ecosystems, including autonomous and semi-autonomous agents, large language models, AI platforms, model gateways, non-human identities, and data access controls. This individual will partner closely with Information Security, Product Security, Legal, Privacy, Engineering, Cloud Operations, Enterprise Architecture, Infrastructure, and business leaders to help drive innovative AI capabilities while protecting customers, products, data, and intellectual property.

Duties & Responsibilities

- Define and lead Itron's enterprise AI security strategy, architecture, policies, standards, reference architectures, and multi-year roadmap.

- Design and implement security controls across the AI and agent lifecycle, including registration, inventory management, identity governance, credential protection, authorization boundaries, autonomy controls, human oversight checkpoints, memory isolation, and agent decommissioning.

- Establish scalable security guardrails for generative AI platforms, model integrations, APIs, plugins, automation workflows, AI assistants, and emerging agentic ecosystems.

- Develop and maintain governance controls supporting privacy, confidentiality, data protection, transparency, explainability, accountability, ethical AI use, and bias mitigation.

- Lead AI-focused threat modeling, adversarial testing, security reviews, and risk assessments for enterprise and customer-facing solutions.

- Evaluate and mitigate emerging AI threats, including prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege escalation, AI supply chain compromise, context poisoning, insecure agent interactions, and rogue agent behavior.

- Partner with engineering, product, and architecture teams to embed secure-by-design principles into the development, deployment, testing, and operation of AI-enabled systems.

- Advance the use of AI within Cybersecurity by designing and piloting AI-assisted capabilities that improve detection engineering, threat hunting, vulnerability management, alert triage, evidence collection, and operational effectiveness.

- Define security logging, telemetry, monitoring, alerting, and reporting requirements that measure AI control effectiveness and detect anomalous or malicious activity.

- Develop and operate AI Security Posture Management capabilities, including inventories, risk assessments, third-party evaluations, incident response processes, compliance readiness, and ongoing monitoring.

- Conduct security assessments of AI vendors, platforms, and service providers with emphasis on architecture, data handling, privacy, access controls, resiliency, and operational risk.

- Provide technical leadership and guidance for AI-related incidents, investigations, governance decisions, policy exceptions, and risk acceptance reviews.

- Author clear technical standards, reference architectures, implementation guidance, and executive communications that enable responsible and secure AI adoption.

- Mentor engineers, architects, and security practitioners while fostering a collaborative, customer-centric culture that balances innovation with risk management.

- Stay current on evolving AI technologies, industry regulations, attack techniques, and emerging security best practices, translating insights into actionable improvements for Itron.

Required Skills & Experience

- 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security architecture, cloud security, identity and access management, application security, product security, or a related technical discipline.

- 2+ years of experience working with AI-enabled systems, machine learning environments, automation platforms, advanced analytics solutions, or generative AI technologies.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience securing or building agentic systems, AI orchestration platforms, non-human identity solutions, model integrations, retrieval pipelines, and automated workflows.

- Experience implementing security controls for cloud platforms, APIs, identity services, secrets management, data protection, logging, monitoring, and third-party integrations.

- Proven experience conducting threat modeling, architecture reviews, security assessments, control validations, and cyber risk evaluations.

- Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, least privilege, secure software design principles, and modern security architectures.

- Ability to analyze complex AI and cybersecurity risks and communicate practical recommendations to both technical and business leaders.

- Exceptional written, verbal, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.

- Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across diverse teams while driving accountability, collaboration, and execution in a fast-changing technology environment.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred Skills & Experience

- Experience securing large-scale deployments of frontier AI models through direct provider APIs, Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, model gateways, or comparable enterprise AI platforms.

- Hands-on experience with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service, Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementations, AI gateway technologies, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Vertex AI, Databricks AI capabilities, ChatGPT Enterprise, or similar platforms.

- Familiarity with AI security and governance frameworks such as NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, MITRE ATLAS, ISO/IEC 42001, and AI regulatory readiness initiatives.

- Experience performing AI red teaming, adversarial testing, prompt injection testing, abuse-case development, or AI deployment readiness assessments.

- Background in secure software development, DevSecOps, CI/CD security, container security, software supply chain security, or product security architecture reviews.

- Experience operating in regulated industries or environments aligned to ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST, GDPR, CMMC, critical infrastructure, utilities, or similar compliance frameworks.

- Professional certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CSSLP, Microsoft Security certifications, cloud security certifications, AI governance certifications, AI security certifications, or equivalent credentials.

Travel: Less than 25% on average
